issue_snapshot.title: Groups and members with invite links and placeholders
issue_snapshot.body:
Friends can create a group, invite by link, claim placeholder seats and manage membership, establishing the authorization boundary.

Person sees: home group list with per-group balance slot, group detail header and settings shell, members-and-invite screen (member list with owner badges, invite panel with copy, disable and rotate, placeholder add-by-name, claim prompts). Contract: DEFINES the groups and memberships schema plus the membership-first authorization pattern every later group route copies: (sessionUser, groupScope, zod-validated input), 401 unauthenticated, 404 when missing or not a member, double-claim of a placeholder rejected. Constraints: TR-7 including non-zero-balance block and membership-scoped visibility; per-request Pool lifecycle applies to all new queries.

**Risk.** Authorization and boundary risk: server-side membership checks on every group read and write, indistinguishable 404s, unguessable invite tokens with disable and rotate, balance-blocked removal.

**Out of scope**
- Expense entry and split math
- Balances, simplification and payments
- Activity feed UI (expense and payment writers land with their own slices)

Covers: TR-3, TR-7, TR-11
Part of #1.
Depends on #4.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Create a group with name, currency and type and see it listed; only members can open it and missing-or-forbidden reads are indistinguishable with no data leak
- **IAC-2** Share an owner invite link, join as a second user, claim a placeholder added by name, and rotate or disable the link with an explicit confirm naming the link
- **IAC-3** Rename, remove, archive and leave flows work with confirms; removal or leave with a non-zero balance is blocked with a message pointing at settle-up

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.

acceptance.check: Signed-in user creates a group (name, currency, type) and sees it in the home group list with its per-group balance slot; opening a group they do not belong to (or that does not exist) returns an indistinguishable 404 with no data leak, and signed-out access redirects to sign-in.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA signs up as user A, creates a group, sees it listed; pastes the URL as signed-out and as user B and gets the same 404 both times.

acceptance.check: Missing-or-forbidden group reads are indistinguishable at the data layer: the membership guard returns 404 whether the group is absent or the caller is a non-member, and unit tests assert both paths carry no group fields.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run lib/groups/authz.test.ts — cases for unknown group id vs valid group as non-member assert identical 404 shape.

acceptance.check: Owner copies an invite link, user B joins through it and claims a placeholder seat added by name, and the owner rotates then disables the link, each behind an explicit confirm naming the link; the pre-rotate link stops working and double-claim of the same placeholder is rejected.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA with two browsers: A creates group, adds placeholder 'Bo', copies link; B joins via /join/<token>, claims 'Bo'; A rotates (old link 404s) then disables (join rejected); B attempts to claim 'Bo' again and is rejected.

acceptance.check: Rename, remove-member, archive and leave flows each require an explicit confirm naming the object; removal or leave with a non-zero balance is blocked with a message pointing at settle-up, and the block is unit-proven through the zero-balance guard seam that TR-9 will later feed with real ledger balances.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA renames, removes a zero-balance member, archives, and leaves as sole flow; unit suite forces a non-zero balance through assertZeroBalance and asserts the settle-up message. Full end-to-end non-zero can only exist once the expense ledger lands (see risks).

acceptance.check: Every group read and write is authorized on the server against the session user via the (sessionUser, groupScope, zod-validated input) pattern: unauthenticated calls get 401/redirect, non-members get 404, invalid input gets a user-safe validation error; negative matrix covered by tests.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run lib/groups/actions.test.ts negative cases (signed-out create, non-member rename/remove/rotate, bad input) plus QA cross-user probe of each group route.

acceptance.check: New screens (home list, group detail header + settings shell, members-and-invite) use only ui.md tokens, keep one h1 with hierarchical headings, labelled controls with visible focus, and designed empty/loading/error states including invite-rotation failure keeping the old link active.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA drives phone and laptop viewports keyboard-only through empty (owner-only group), loading (skeleton members), error (failed rotate keeps old link) states.

alternatives_considered.approach: Separate invite_tokens table (one row per link, many active links per group)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: TR-7 and ui.md describe a single link panel with copy/disable/rotate; one token+enabled flag on the group is the smallest shape that satisfies it, and a table with one row per group is abstraction without a caller.

alternatives_considered.approach: Claim-by-email-match only (a placeholder is claimable solely by the user whose email or display name matches it)
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue text promises 'claim prompts for matching placeholders' but the repo has no verified identity beyond email, and strict matching would strand seats on typos; open seat-pick with server-side double-claim rejection is testable now, and matching hints stay UI-only.

validated_work_order.approach: Add the groups authorization boundary in one ticket: groups + memberships tables (TRD data model), a membership-first guard every group call copies, Server Actions for create/rename/remove/archive/leave/invite-rotate-disable/placeholder-add/claim/join-by-token, and the three screens (home list with balance slot, group detail header + settings shell, members-and-invite). All DB work goes through withDb so the Neon Pool opens and closes per request (binding route-note invariant), no code outside lib/db/client.ts branches on backend, and money-adjacent rules stay integer-minor-unit pure functions. The non-zero-balance block ships as an enforced guard call with a documented seam: with no expense/payment ledger yet every balance is definitionally zero, and unit tests force non-zero through the seam to prove the message points at settle-up until TR-9 feeds it real balances.
assumptions: Any signed-in member may add a placeholder by name; only the owner may rename, remove members, archive, rotate or disable the invite link.
Placeholder claim is open seat-pick by a signed-in user, not email/name match; the server rejects double-claim atomically and rejects claims by users already in the group.
Group type is the closed TRD set trip/home/couple/other and currency reuses SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES (INR default from profile).
Archive hides the group from the home list but members can still open it (read-only banner); removal here means member-row delete, not group delete.
Invite token is 32 bytes CSPRNG base64url stored unique; disable flips invite_enabled, rotate issues a fresh token and the old one stops working.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Approach maps 1:1 onto the TRD data model and the issue contract, and I independently verified every load-bearing claim against the code: the withDb/getSessionUser pattern (app/page.tsx, lib/auth/session.ts), the per-request Pool lifecycle with close-on-error (lib/db/client.ts withDb/finally plus remoteHandle pool.end), the backend-invariant scan (lib/db/backend-invariant.test.ts), SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES with INR default (lib/auth/validation.ts, 0002 migration), and the guarded hand-written migration convention with 0003 as the correct next number. Held at 72 because the non-zero-balance block cannot be proven end-to-end until the expense ledger exists, placeholder-claim identity policy is a judgment call the issue leaves open, and round 2 filed no critique, so the adversarial pass is my own rather than independent.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: Round 2 produced no critique: plan/critique.json is literally {} (no verdict, no findings, no edge cases), so there was nothing to judge, adopt, or dismiss. Per the arbiter brief I did the critic's verification myself instead of treating the proposal's word as final: re-grepped the withDb/getDb/getSessionUser callers, read lib/db/client.ts, schema.ts, migrate.ts, backend-invariant.test.ts, both shipped migrations, lib/auth/validation.ts and session.ts, and app/page.tsx. All verifiable claims held: the copied auth pattern exists, the Pool opens and closes per request even on error, no code outside the client branches on backend, the currency constants and INR default exist, and 0003 follows the guarded hand-written convention. The brief binds nothing against the plan: its two route notes on epic #1 are already satisfied in code, there is no rejected plan for issue #5, and the proposal touches no forbidden path. One gap the absent critic could not find: join-by-token when the caller is already a member was unspecified, so I added a safe-no-op case to actions.test.ts. Everything else is kept as proposed; no finding was dismissed because none was filed.
evidence: lib/db/client.ts:119-126 withDb closes the handle in finally however fn ends; remoteHandle pool.end at 96-99 — per-request Pool lifecycle already in code.
app/page.tsx:12 and lib/auth/session.ts:145 getSessionUser(db) — the (sessionUser, withDb) pattern the plan copies.
lib/db/backend-invariant.test.ts:21-59 scan fails the build on any backend reference outside lib/db/client.ts.
lib/auth/validation.ts:24 SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES with INR default; 0002 migration sets users.currency DEFAULT INR.
lib/db/migrations/: 0001 ledger + 0002 auth shipped, so 0003_groups_memberships.sql is the correct next number; schema.ts header mandates guarded hand-written SQL with no ledger DDL.
plan/critique.json is {} — no verdict or findings filed; plan/brief.md records no rejected plan for issue #5 and its two route notes are satisfied without docs changes.

files.change: Add groups table (id, name, currency, type, invite_token unique nullable, invite_enabled default true, archived default false, timestamps) and memberships table (id, group_id FK cascade, user_id FK nullable, display_name, role owner/member, timestamps) with unique (group_id, user_id) and index on invite_token.
files.why: TRD data model for TR-7: the authorization boundary every later ticket builds on.

files.change: Hand-written guarded migration (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + indexes, breakpoint-separated, no ledger DDL) for groups/memberships; immutable filename once applied.
files.why: Same migrations on PGlite and Neon via the shared runner; hand-written per the schema.ts header rule.

files.change: Zod boundary schemas: createGroup, renameGroup, addPlaceholder, joinByToken, claimPlaceholder; trim/normalize at the boundary like auth validation.
files.why: Membership-first pattern requires zod-validated input at the route/action boundary.

files.change: Pure helpers: generateInviteToken (randomBytes 32 base64url); no DB or env reads, backend-agnostic.
files.why: Unguessable invite tokens with rotate/disable semantics in one testable place.

files.change: Membership-first guard: guardGroup resolves session user (401) then membership row (404 whether missing or non-member); requireOwner builds on it. No backend branching.
files.why: The contract every later group route copies, with indistinguishable 404s.

files.change: Pure removal rules: assertZeroBalance throws the settle-up message when non-zero; getMemberBalance seam returning 0 with a documented TR-9 replacement point.
files.why: Non-zero-balance block enforced at call sites now though the ledger arrives later.

files.change: Server Actions via withDb: createGroup, renameGroup, archiveGroup, removeMember, leaveGroup, addPlaceholder, claimPlaceholder (atomic, reject double-claim), joinByToken, rotateInvite, disableInvite; revalidatePath on mutation.
files.why: All group writes in one audited module following the auth withDb pattern (per-request Pool close).

files.change: Home screen regions: totals placeholder, group list with per-group balance slot (zero/pending until TR-9), empty state with create button, error with retry; signed-out prompt unchanged.
files.why: Home group list with per-group balance slot from the issue contract.

files.change: Server page with create-group form posting to createGroup; inline errors, input preserved on failure.
files.why: Group creation entry point for IAC-1.

files.change: Server page: group header, balance banner shell, settings section (rename/archive with confirms naming the group); non-member/missing renders shared 404.
files.why: Group detail header and settings shell.

files.change: Server page: member list with owner badges, invite-link panel, placeholder add-by-name, claim prompts; ui.md loading/partial/error states.
Server page resolving token to group (404 when unknown/disabled), join + claim choice for signed-in users (redirect to signin preserving token).
Client islands only: invite-panel (copy, disable/rotate with confirm naming the link) and members-panel (removes/leave/archive confirms, claim buttons, toasts + aria-live); tokens-only styling.
files.why: Interactive islands for clipboard and confirms; pages stay Server Components.

qa_script: Sign up as A, create group 'Goa trip' (INR, trip), assert it lists with a balance slot.
As A: Members screen shows owner badge; add placeholder 'Bo' by name.
Copy invite link; open it signed-out and assert redirect to signin, then as B join and claim 'Bo'; assert member list shows B and placeholder gone.
As B attempt to claim 'Bo' again and assert rejection.
As A rotate the link with the confirm naming the link; open the old link as C and assert expired; disable the link and assert join is rejected.
Rename, archive, remove zero-balance member and leave flows each show a confirm naming the object; assert the balance-block message points at settle-up when the guard trips.
residual_risks: Placeholder-claim concurrency: sequential double-claim is unit-proven, but two users claiming the same seat at once relies on the implementer making the claim update atomic at the row level.

Membership changes write no activity rows in this ticket (no ActivityEvent table exists yet); the later activity ticket must decide whether member join/leave/remove events are recorded or backfilled, since a project invariant assumes they are.
Archive enforcement is hidden-from-list plus a read-only banner; server-side write guards on archived groups beyond the banner are left to implementer judgment.

No independent critic reviewed this plan (critique.json empty); the adversarial pass above is the arbiter's own, so an implementer reading lib/groups/actions.ts fresh should still sanity-check the guard ordering.
risks: End-to-end non-zero-balance blocking cannot exist until the expense/payment ledger does: the guard and message are enforced and unit-proven, but QA cannot drive a real non-zero balance on this ticket alone.
Placeholder claim is seat-pick, not identity-matched: a joiner could claim the wrong seat; mitigated by owner removal + double-claim rejection, match-by-email layerable later without schema change.
Invite token column is nullable-unique per TRD: multiple NULLs permitted, so disable/rotate races rely on the enabled flag + single owner path rather than the constraint alone.

cases: createGroup rejects blank name, bad currency, bad type with field errors
addPlaceholder rejects blank/overlong names; joinByToken rejects empty token
unknown group id vs valid group as non-member return identical 404 shape with no group fields
signed-out caller gets 401; owner check rejects plain member for rotate/rename/remove/archive
assertZeroBalance passes on 0 and throws the settle-up-pointing message on non-zero
double-claim of a placeholder is rejected; claim by an existing member is rejected
create then list shows the group to the member only; non-member list excludes it
join by token adds membership; rotated token invalidates the old link; disabled link rejects join
remove/leave calls the zero-balance guard; migration 0003 applies cleanly on PGlite
join by token when already a member is a safe no-op with no duplicate membership row

validated_work_order.understanding: Issue #5 builds the groups authorization boundary: group CRUD (name, currency, type), owner invite links with copy/disable/rotate, placeholder seats added by name and claimed on join, member management with confirms, and removal/leave blocked on non-zero balance — every group read/write gated server-side on membership with indistinguishable 404s, following the (sessionUser, groupScope, zod-validated input) contract. plan/brief.md records no rejected plan for this issue (nothing to answer), and its two route notes on epic #1 are already satisfied in code: lib/db/client.ts opens the neon-serverless Pool per request and closes it via withDb even on error, and lib/db/backend-invariant.test.ts forbids backend branching outside the client — so this plan complies with both without touching forbidden docs paths. Grepped all withDb/getDb/getSessionUser callers and this plan copies that exact pattern. Balances and expenses are out of scope, so the non-zero guard ships as an enforced seam TR-9 will feed.
unknowns: Should archive make the group read-only or merely hide it from the home list? Chosen: hidden from list, openable with a read-only banner.
Should placeholder add suggest matching by display-name similarity at claim time? Chosen: UI hint only, no server matching rule.
Exact group-name length cap: TRD is silent; chosen 1–80 chars mirroring the auth display-name rule.
